pattern_explanation: Each Portuguese word looks similar to an English word but has a different meaning, so the English look-alike is the trap.
false_friend_warning: The Portuguese word 'constipado' means having a cold, but the English word 'constipated' means unable to pass stools. The Portuguese word 'pretender' means to intend, while the English word 'pretend' means to act as if something is true. The Portuguese word 'assistir' means to watch or attend, while the English word 'assist' means to help. The Portuguese word 'esquisito' means strange, while the English word 'exquisite' means extremely beautiful or refined. Students should check the meaning in context before using any of these look-alikes.
